narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist; sober, urgent storytelling, grave through the Passion.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; authoritative and prophetic in ch. 13, sorrowful yet resolute in the Passion, commanding after the Resurrection.

disciples.name: The disciples
disciples.note: Jesus' followers; earnest questions, then dismay at the supper.

chief-priests.name: The chief priests
chief-priests.note: Temple leaders, here speaking together with the scribes; scheming in private, mocking at the cross.

indignant-guests.name: Indignant guests at Bethania
indignant-guests.note: Some at table in Simon's house, grumbling at the waste of the ointment.

peter.name: Peter
peter.note: Simon Peter; vehement in his promises, frightened and blustering in his denials.

judas.name: Judas Iscariot
judas.note: The betrayer; low and furtive giving the sign, falsely warm in his greeting.

false-witnesses.name: False witnesses
false-witnesses.note: Men testifying against Jesus before the council; assertive but inconsistent.

high-priest.name: The high priest
high-priest.note: Presides over the council; imperious, then theatrically outraged.

council-members.name: Members of the council
council-members.note: Some of those who condemned Jesus, jeering as they strike him blindfolded.

servant-girl.name: Maid-servant of the high priest
servant-girl.note: A servant in the courtyard; sharp and accusing as she recognises Peter.

bystanders.name: Bystanders
bystanders.note: Those standing by: pressing Peter in the courtyard; mishearing Jesus' cry at the cross.

1.t: Now the feast of the Pasch, and of the azymes, was after two days: and the chief priests, and the Scribes, sought how they might by craft lay hold on him, and kill him.

2.t: Not on the festival day, lest there should be a tumult among the people.
2.q: spoken by the chief priests and the scribes together (14:1)

3.t: And when he was in Bethania, in the house of Simon, the leper, and was at meat; there came a woman, having an alabaster-box of ointment of precious spikenard, and breaking the alabaster-box, she poured it out upon his head.

4.t: Now there were some that had indignation within themselves, and said:
Why was this waste of the ointment made?

5.t: For this ointment might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and given to the poor.

6.t: Let her alone; why do you molest her? She hath wrought a good work upon me.

7.t: For the poor you have always with you; and whensoever you will, you may do them good: but me you have not always.

8.t: What she had she hath done: she is come beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.

9.t: Amen, I say to you, wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, that also which she hath done, shall be told for a memorial of her.

10.t: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests, to betray him to them.

11.t: They hearing it, were glad: and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.

12.t: Now, on the first day of the unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Pasch, the disciples say to him:
Whither wilt thou that we go, and prepare for thee to eat the Pasch?

13.t: And he sendeth two of his disciples, and saith to them:
Go ye into the city: and there shall meet you a man carrying a pitcher of water, follow him;

14.t: And wheresoever he shall go in, say to the master of the house: The master saith, Where is my refectory: where I may eat the Pasch with my disciples?

15.t: And he will shew you a large dining-room, furnished: and there prepare ye for us.

16.t: And his disciples went their way, and came into the city: and they found as he had told them, and they prepared the Pasch.

17.t: And when evening was come, he cometh with the twelve.

18.t: And when they were at table, and eating, Jesus saith:
Amen, I say to you, that one of you who eateth with me, shall betray me.

19.t: But they began to be sorrowful, and to say to him one by one:

19.q: said by each disciple in turn, not in unison

20.t: One of the twelve who dippeth his hand in the dish with me.

21.t: And the Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but wo to that man, by whom the Son of man shall be betrayed. It were better for him, if that man had not been born.

22.t: And whilst they were eating, Jesus took bread: and blessing, broke, and gave to them, and said:
Take ye, This is my body.

23.t: And having taken the chalice, giving thanks, he gave to them, and they all drank of it.

24.t: This is my blood of the New Testament, which shall be shed for many.

25.t: Amen, I say unto you, that I will drink no more of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it new in the kingdom of God.

26.t: And when they had sung a hymn, they went forth to the mount of Olives.

27.t: You will all be scandalized in me this night: for it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be dispersed;

28.t: But after I shall be risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

29.t: Although all shall be scandalized in thee, yet not I.

30.t: Amen, I say to thee, to-day, even in this night, before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.

31.t: But he spoke the more vehemently:
Although I should die together with thee, I will not deny thee:
And in like manner also said they all.

32.t: And they came to a farm called Gethsemani. And he saith to his disciples:
Sit you here while I pray.

33.t: And he taketh Peter and James, and John, with him; and he began to fear, and to be heavy.

34.t: My soul is sorrowful even unto death: stay you here and watch.

35.t: And when he had gone forward a little, he fell flat on the ground: and he prayed, that, if it could be, the hour might pass from him:

36.t: Abba, Father, all things are possible to thee; take away this chalice from me: but not what I will, but what thou wilt.

37.t: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping. And he saith to Peter:
Simon, sleepest thou? couldst thou not watch one hour?

38.t: Watch ye, and pray that you enter not into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

39.t: A going away again, he prayed, saying the same words.

40.t: And when he returned, he found them again asleep, (for their eyes were heavy) and they knew not what to answer him.

41.t: And he cometh the third time, and saith to them:
Sleep ye now, and take your rest. It is enough: the hour is come: behold the Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of sinners.

42.t: Rise up: let us go. Behold, he that will betray me, is at hand.

43.t: And while he was yet speaking, cometh Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve: and with him a great multitude, with swords and staves, from the chief priests, and the Scribes, and the ancients.

44.t: And he that betrayed him had given them a sign, saying:
Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he, lay hold on him, and lead him away cautiously.

45.t: And when he was come, immediately going up to him, he saith:

46.t: But they laid hands on him, and held him.

47.t: An one of them that stood by drawing a sword, struck a servant of the chief priest, and cut off his ear.

48.t: And Jesus answering, said to them:
are you come out as against a robber with swords and staves to apprehend me?

49.t: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and you did not lay hands on me. But, that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.

50.t: Then his disciples leaving him, all fled away.

51.t: And a certain young man followed him, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body: and they laid hold on him.

52.t: But he casting off the linen cloth, fled from them naked.

53.t: And they brought Jesus to the high priest: and all the priests, and the Scribes, and the ancients, assembled together.

54.t: And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants at the fire, and warmed himself.

55.t: And the chief priests, and all the council, sought for evidence against Jesus, that they might put him to death; and they found none.

56.t: For many bore false witness against him, and their evidence did not agree.

57.t: And some rising up, bore false witness against him, saying:

58.t: We heard him say: I will destroy this temple made with hands, and within three days I will build another, not made with hands.

59.t: And their witness did not agree.

60.t: And the high priest rising up in the midst, asked Jesus, saying:
Answerest thou nothing to the things that are laid to thy charge by these men?

61.t: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said to him:
Art thou the Christ, the Son of the blessed God?

62.t: I am: And you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God, and coming with the clouds of heaven.

63.t: Then the high priest rending his garments, saith:
What need we any farther witnesses?

64.t: You have heard the blasphemy. What think you?
They all condemned him to be guilty of death.

65.t: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say to him:

65.q: the "some" who mock are taken as members of the council that just condemned him

65.t: and the servants struck him with the palms of their hands.

66.t: Now, when Peter was in the court below, there cometh one of the maid-servants of the high priest:

67.t: And when she had seen Peter warming himself, looking on him, she saith:
Thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.

68.t: I neither know nor understand what thou sayest.
And he went forth before the court; and the cock crew.

69.t: And again a maid-servant seeing him, began to say to the standers-by:

69.q: text says "a maid-servant"; taken as the same maid as 14:66-67 (Matthew has another maid)

70.t: But he denied again. And after a while they that stood by, said again to Peter:
Surely thou art one of them: for thou art also a Galilean.

71.t: But he began to curse and to swear, saying;
I know not this man of whom you speak.

72.t: And immediately the cock crew again. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him:
Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.
72.q: Jesus' earlier words (14:30) recalled by Peter inside narration; given to Jesus as a remembered voice, could be narrator
